text:
The Blackhawks are supposed to be in a hole right now. Connor Bedard is out about four months after surgery, as Flames Nation and others reported this week, and Wyatt Kaiser is serving a three-game suspension. Instead Chicago has won four straight, and Friday's 2-1 win over the Rangers was the strangest of them: the Blackhawks put 10 shots on goal all night.

Everything that mattered happened in the first period, and all of it on the power play. Andrew Mangiapane snapped one in at 4:23, set up by Oliver Moore. Mika Zibanejad tied it at 17:41 with J.T. Miller and Adam Fox assisting. Then, 86 seconds later, Mangiapane scored again, Moore and Ryan Donato on the play, and Chicago led 2-1 at the break despite trailing 10-3 in shots, according to The Athletic's Scott Powers. Chicago went 2 for 2 with the man advantage on 0.29 expected goals, which is about as efficient as a power play gets.

After that it was Spencer Knight against the Rangers. New York outattempted Chicago 71 to 25 and won the third period 1.67 to 0.11 in expected goals (the quality of chances, added up). Knight stopped 30 of 31 and saved about two goals more than those shots deserved, the biggest a 24% chance for Max Sasson, newly acquired from Vancouver, in the third. His 0.58 wins added led everyone by a distance. The Blackhawks also blocked 22 shots to the Rangers' five, which tells you where the puck lived. Powers put the crowd at 20,302, Chicago's biggest of the season.

Be honest about what this was: our replays of every shot gave the Rangers the win 80% of the time. Chicago's streak is real in the standings, and Knight is a big part of why, but a team that gets outshot 31 to 10 at home is living on its goalie. For Mike Sullivan's Rangers, already missing Pavel Dorofeyev, and with Yahoo Sports reporting Smits and Bjorkstrand out two to three months, it is the second kind of frustrating loss: the kind where you did most things right and Dylan Garand faced only 10 shots and still lost.
headline: Ten shots, two goals, four straight: Knight carries Chicago
